record.paper_title: Negative Circles in Signed Graphs: A Problem Collection
record.original_question: Given a signed graph Σ and an edge e, determine whether e lies in a unique positive circle of Σ.

evidence.quote: EP3. In Σ, is a certain edge e in a unique positive circle? Ans. It should broadly resemble E3 but have distinctive features.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A signed graph is a pair Σ = (G, σ) where G = (V, E) is a finite undirected graph (loops and multiple edges allowed) and σ : E → {+1, −1} is a sign function on its edges. A circle (also called a cycle or circuit) of Σ is the edge set of a simple closed walk in G. The sign of a circle C is the product ∏_{e ∈ C} σ(e); the circle is called positive if this product equals +1 and negative otherwise.

Problem. Design an algorithm that, given as input a signed graph Σ = (G, σ) and a distinguished edge e ∈ E(G), decides whether e lies in exactly one positive circle of Σ. Equivalently, characterize structurally those triples (G, σ, e) for which there is a unique positive circle of Σ containing e, and determine the computational complexity of recognizing this property.
artifact.status_search_result: A 2017 paper "Edges and vertices in a unique signed circle in a signed graph" (Akiyama, Avadayappan, et al., AKCE J. Graphs Combin.) characterizes structurally when an edge of a signed graph lies in a unique positive (or negative) circle, describing the underlying graph structure via bridges of a circle and giving distinct signature conditions for the positive and negative cases. This addresses the structural recognition asked here, though the original problem collection asked also for features distinguishing the positive case from the negative one, which the follow-up partly resolves.

status_evidence.title: Edges and vertices in a unique signed circle in a signed graph
status_evidence.snippet: For an edge in a unique signed circle, the positive and negative case require the same structure on the underlying graph, but the requirements on the signature are different; the structure is characterized in terms of bridges of a circle.
status_evidence.claim: The question of whether an edge of a signed graph lies in a unique positive circle has been characterized structurally.

status_evidence.title: Negative (and positive) circles in signed graphs: A problem collection
status_evidence.snippet: EP3. In Σ, is a certain edge e in a unique positive circle? It should broadly resemble E3 but have distinctive features.
status_evidence.claim: The problem appears as an explicit open question in Zaslavsky's problem collection.
